purpose: Reference review evidence, not additional selected generation inputs

sources.citation: Dalton et al. (2023), NADI-1 v1; Quaternary Science Reviews 321, 108345
sources.evidence: Publisher supplies regional Innuitian, Cordilleran and Laurentide optimal/minimum/maximum extents. Compare all three pinned 12 ka layers via independent OGR/GDAL transfer checks.
sources.independence: Same reconstruction as input; validates transfer and declared scope, not independent geological accuracy.

sources.locator: 12 ka discussion; Younger Dryas discussion; Figure 1 caption
sources.evidence: The 12 ka reconstruction follows the late Younger Dryas Scandinavian margin, with central and maximum lines tied to different Salpausselka moraines in Finland. Small peripheral glaciers are omitted. Published map backdrops use modern coastlines, so they cannot validate paleo shorelines.
sources.independence: Published description of selected reconstruction; qualitative geographic check only.

sources.citation: Godbout, Brouard and Roy (2023), Scientific Data 10, 735
sources.locator: Paleotopographic reconstructions, Figure 3 caption, Technical Validation
sources.evidence: Epoch-relative paleoDEM zero denotes predicted coastline only outside ice and connected to ocean. Model differences reflect loading histories; interpolation validation does not establish shoreline accuracy. Published illustration is 10 ka, not this 12 ka source slice.
sources.independence: Methods validation of selected terrain; no independent 12 ka shoreline geometry or absolute accuracy threshold.

sources.citation: Jakobsson et al. (2017), Climate of the Past 13, 991-1005
sources.evidence: Herald Canyon core evidence suggests Bering Strait opening around 11 cal ka BP, while earlier studies proposed Younger Dryas dates. At 11.949 ka this motivates checking exposed Beringia, but does not settle an exact shoreline or human traversability.
sources.independence: Independent regional evidence; Bering Strait is outside the selected terrain domain, so mask comparison is unavailable.

sources.citation: Walker et al. (2020), A great wave: the Storegga tsunami and the end of Doggerland?, Antiquity
sources.locator: Figure 2: North Sea reconstructions at 10, 9, 8.2 and 7 cal ka BP
sources.evidence: These younger reconstructions identify the southern North Sea as a relevant land-bridge review region. They are not an exact 11.949 ka coastline and are not substituted for a selected Eurasian terrain model.
sources.independence: Independent but younger evidence; the delivered coastline candidates have no Eurasian support.
